_doc: Placeable ship components. Content is data: add an entry here and it can be placed. size is [w, h] in cells at rotation 0 (a crew body is 2x2 cells, so a 1-cell corridor is too narrow). power: positive produces, negative consumes. priority: lower is powered first when power is short (0 for producers and zero-power parts). tier: 1 to 3 (Mk1 to Mk3). family groups related parts. manned: works better with crew. stats: numbers read by the systems that use the part. line: scrap, standard or neon (data/lines.json). hp: system health, at 0 it is disabled until repaired. heat_limit: overheats at this heat. heat_per_s: heat gained per second while running. cooling: heat lost per second. stats.cooling_bonus: extra cooling every part in the same room gets (radiator). Shield stats: stats.layers (bubble layers), stats.sectors (1, 2, 4 or 8: how many sectors the bubble is split into, bow first and clockwise: Mk1 and scrap 1, Mk2 2, Mk3 and Neon 4, and 8 for the Mk5 and the late uniques; the best powered generator sets it, and each sector holds layers x its balance weight, docs/CONTENT.md section 4) and stats.recharge (seconds until a used layer is back, default 2.0; lower is faster: Abilities.recharge_rate scales the shield's recharge by 2.0 / stats.recharge, 1.4 is 1.43 times as fast). unique: true marks a found-or-traded item that has no recipe. effects: tags the combat code reads for a unique or special part (for weapons they live in weapons.json). A weapon part needs an entry in weapons.json under the same id. abilities: optional list of {id, name, type (active or passive), key (engine, shield or utility: the combat key that triggers an active one), duration and cooldown in seconds (the cooldown starts when the effect ends), effects, side_effects, operator_needs, event} (see docs/CONTENT.md section 5 and scripts/sim/abilities.gd). effects: stat_mult {thrust or power: factor} on this part, shield_layer (extra layers), charge_mult (weapon cooldown factor), evasion_add. side_effects: a list of {type, rate} applied per second while it runs: drain_o2 (fraction of the room's air lost per second), heat, power_spike (extra draw), fire_risk (chance per second), self_damage (hp per second). Racial keys (docs/CONTENT.md section 17, scripts/sim/part_effects.gd; "room" is the room of the part's anchor, "up" crew are neither downed nor stunned, `who` is a species id, a trait id or "mechanical", "a|b" either): effects.crew_bonus {who, stat (power, thrust or shield_layer), per, max} adds per up crew member in the room matching who, up to max in all (power to the part's output, thrust to the engine's thrust, layers to a shield, rounded down); effects.crew_needed {count, stat (power, thrust, shield_layer, recharge or evasion), else_mult, who?} multiplies the stat by else_mult unless count up crew (matching who) stand in the room (layers round down; recharge is the speed shield layers come back at, 0.5 = twice as long; evasion is the ability's own evasion_add); both may be a list of entries; effects.room_wall_hp_mult: factor on the hp of the wall cells round the room, set when a fight starts (the strongest on a cell counts); effects.heat_above {heat, shield_layer}: that many extra layers while the room's hottest part is above heat; effects.room_work_mult {mult, who?, else_mult?}: factor on the work speed (repair, extinguish, breach, revive) of crew in the room, mult for those matching who, else_mult (default 1) for the rest; side_effects shock_organic (rate = hp per second to every crew member in the room who is not mechanical), scorch (rate = hp per second to every crew member in the room without the heat_resistant trait: the mirror of shock_organic, so an Emberkin crew runs a hot part free; the part's own heat is the separate heat side effect) and wet (rate = work factor, e.g. 0.8, for crew in the room unless their work_mult.extinguish is above 1; every part in the room also loses 30 heat at the start of each second). shield_layer and recharge effects only work on a shield part. The validator is PartEffects.problems / component_problems (tests/test_components.gd). stats.malfunction_per_min (a chance per minute, 0 to 1) overrides the line's malfunction rate for that part. operator_needs: traits a crew member manning the part must have; a|b means either. blurb: one line of flavour. Ram parts (docs/CONTENT.md 4e) read stats.ram_deal (damage dealt to the other ship in a collision, as a multiple), stats.tether_s (seconds it latches on after a hit), stats.ram_take (multiple of ram damage taken by the ship's plain cells while the part is powered) and stats.no_knock (1: crew take no knock from a ram while it is powered). mount (weapons and engines): {outside: [w, h], outside_hp} makes the part two linked halves through a hull wall of any thickness (docs/CONTENT.md 4f). size is the INSIDE half (on the floor, crewed and wired); the outside half sits in space at the outer wall face, outward is UP at rotation 0, takes the visible hits with its own outside_hp and is only ever disabled (a weapon's outside_hp is twice its hp, an armoured barrel housing that the crew can patch between volleys; an engine's or an intake's is 75% of its hp, rounded); a direct hit on a disabled inside half wrecks the part. Engine stats: thrust, and fuel_mult (a jump of the Drift costs 1 x the thrust-weighted mean fuel_mult of the powered engines; an engine without one counts as 1.0; docs/waves/engines_1.md). quirk: a line of text saying why a part is off its balance band (data/balance.json), which exempts it.

components.name: Reactor Mk1
components.blurb: Standard fusion core, certified safe. Certification pending since the Snap.

components.name: Reactor Mk2
components.blurb: More output, same footprint, same warranty. The warranty office is closed.

components.name: Concord Thruster Mk1
components.blurb: Reliable thrust, uncomplicated. Do not mistake that for exciting.

components.name: Concord Thruster Mk2
components.blurb: Improved thrust, improved paperwork. Mostly the paperwork.

components.name: Afterburner
components.blurb: Burns the engine room's air along with the fuel. Man it in a suit, and keep the door shut.

components.name: Oxygen Generator
components.blurb: Scrubs, cracks and recirculates. Output meets regulation. The regulation was set low, by tired people.

components.name: Shield Mk1
components.blurb: A single bubble of certified safety. Certification not valid in the Drift.

components.name: Laser Mk1
components.blurb: Standard-issue beam. Does what it says on the form.

components.name: Laser Mk2
components.blurb: Second revision of the standard beam. The revision notes are longer than the beam.

components.name: Concord Point Turret
components.blurb: A swivelling laser that tracks and fires by itself. Reliable chip damage for crews who would rather fly than aim.

components.name: Helm
components.blurb: One chair, one wheel, one person to blame.

components.name: Medbay
components.blurb: Sterile, bright and optimistic. Staff should have soft hands; Basalt staff are reminded they do not.

components.name: Bed
components.blurb: Bunk, thin mattress, one blanket. 'Crew' are not issued a second blanket.

components.name: Fabricator
components.blurb: Turns materials and blueprints into parts, and waiting lists into queues.

components.name: Robot Arm
components.blurb: Workshop module. Raises the Fabricator to level 2 and holds things steady while you swear at them.

components.name: Laser Cutter
components.blurb: Workshop module. Cuts plate cleanly; the manual notes it will also cut the manual.

components.name: Assembly Rig
components.blurb: Workshop module. Three arms, one frame, and a safety guide read in full by nobody.

components.name: Nanoforge
components.blurb: Workshop module, level 4. Builds from the atom up. Please do not ask what with.

components.name: Rustbucket Reactor
components.blurb: Cheap salvage core. Loud, thirsty and it hiccups.

components.name: Kickjet
components.blurb: Welded together from three other engines. Kicks like a mule.

components.name: Wheezer O2
components.blurb: Wheezes, rattles and keeps you breathing. Mostly.

components.name: Prism Core
components.blurb: Crystal lattice reactor. Huge output, runs very hot: bring radiators.

components.name: Ion Drive: Glimmer
components.blurb: Light and fast, glows when it works.

components.name: Radiator
components.blurb: Dumps heat to space. Adds cooling to every part in its room.

components.name: Pulse Mk1
components.blurb: A steady thump of plasma. Honest work, slightly dull.

components.name: Pulse Mk2
components.blurb: Same thump, bigger fist. Dents hulls and egos alike.

components.name: Rattle Burst
components.blurb: A little auto turret that rattles out one cheap round after another, if it doesn't seize up first.

components.name: Shrapnel Cannon
components.blurb: Spits a fistful of scrap at everything at once. Shields hate it.

components.name: Bolt Thrower
components.blurb: Eats scrap and throws it back with feeling. Never dry while the hold has junk.

components.name: Artemis Mk1
components.blurb: Guided and polite about it: sails through shields, then goes off.

components.name: Ion Blast
components.blurb: Harmless to the hull, ruinous to the shields. Everything it touches goes quiet.

components.name: Siren Ion
components.blurb: Wails across the target ship, and its doors lock up in sympathy.

components.name: Heat Lance
components.blurb: A beam that sets rooms on fire as a hobby. Runs hot enough to cook itself.

components.name: Leech Laser
components.blurb: Every hit sips the enemy reactor and hands you the change.

components.name: Breach Harpoon
components.blurb: Punches a hole and leaves a rope behind. Reels derelicts in for docking.

components.name: Bubble Rig
components.blurb: A bubble held together with hope and tape. Flickers.

components.name: Shield Mk2
components.blurb: Two layers of standard-issue peace of mind.

components.name: Neon Lattice Shield
components.blurb: Two layers that snap back fast. Pray nobody brings an ion gun.

components.name: Mirror Veil
components.blurb: Bounces the odd bolt back at whoever sent it.

components.name: Inertial Dampener
components.blurb: Soaks up the shock of a ram. Half damage to your plain cells and the crew keep their feet. Needs power.

components.name: Battering Bow
components.blurb: A Scrapper wedge of welded girders. Triple ram damage, and it latches on to whatever it hits.

components.name: Ma's Kettle
components.blurb: Ma Gantry's own reactor, handed over with a straight face. Two more power than it has any right to, and the room smells of tea and smoke.

components.name: Net Mouth
components.blurb: A hoop of cable and fishing wire bolted over a hole. Debris that touches the net is hauled in. No power, no manners.

components.name: Salvage Intake Mk1
components.blurb: A magnetic mouth and a sorting hopper. Pulls in what drifts within two cells and files it as cargo.

components.name: Ammo Rack
components.blurb: Four bays, a clamp and a hand-lettered sign saying NOT A SEAT. Holds twenty rounds of one kind, and wants them all to stay put.
components.quirk: Guns in its room (or on its belt) draw from it. Crew restock it from the cargo below half full. If it is wrecked while holding missiles, it explodes.

components.name: Clan Chain Drive
components.blurb: A bicycle chain the length of a corridor, a motor off a garbage lift and a sign: KICK TO START. The Clans swear by it.
components.quirk: 3 cells a second, one unit every 0.8 s. Like every Scrap part it jams (malfunctions) now and then, and the belt stops until a crew member kicks it.

components.name: Concord Autoloader
components.blurb: Registered, certified and quiet. A spoked wheel turns in a window, and the rounds go where the form says they go.
components.quirk: 5 cells a second, one unit every 0.5 s. Nothing clever.

components.name: Lumen Mag-Rail
components.blurb: A rail of lit glass that carries each round on a cushion of light, faster than you can follow it. Faint, humming, and allergic to ion.
components.quirk: 8 cells a second, one unit every 0.3 s. Neon: an ion hit shuts it (and the belt) down twice as long as it does the other drives.

components.name: Salvage Intake Mk2
components.blurb: A wider mouth with two coils a cheek and a second belt in the hopper. Draws in what drifts within four cells.

components.name: Salvage Intake Mk3
components.blurb: Heavy rims, three fat coils a cheek and a field stabiliser. Hauls in what drifts within five cells, and drinks more power doing it.

components.name: Radar Mk1
components.blurb: A dish on a turntable outside and a small round scope inside. Shows a contact and its bearing out to 6,000 px, but not what it is.

components.name: Radar Mk2
components.blurb: A bigger dish and a wide console. Sees 10,000 px, names what it sees, and rates how dangerous a ship is in skulls.

components.name: Radar Mk3
components.blurb: A phased array on a boom. Sees 16,000 px, names what it sees, and finds the contacts that are running dark.

components.name: Tractor Beam Mk1
components.blurb: A bank of copper coils behind a swivelling emitter. Hold Q and it hauls the debris within 300 px toward the nearest working intake.

components.name: Tractor Beam Mk2
components.blurb: Five coils and a flared emitter. Hold Q and it hauls the debris within 450 px toward the nearest intake, faster than the Mk1.
